items.title: British Pound futures rise on Bank of England rate expectations.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino analyzes the recent performance of British Pound futures, which formed an inside range day to finish higher against the U.S. dollar. Despite U.K. fiscal concerns and the 30-year gilt yield climbing to its highest level since 1998 ahead of the October 28 autumn budget, expectations for further Bank of England tightening continue to support the currency. Traders now look ahead to upcoming speeches from Monetary Policy Committee member Catherine Mann and Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey for signals on a potential November rate hike.

items.title: Surging Treasury yields and Fed minutes put markets on watch.
items.excerpt: Treasury yields enter the week in focus after the 2-Year yield surged 54 bps and the 5-Year jumped 61 bps in September. Focus turns to Wednesday's FOMC minutes, which will detail the central bank's first rate hike since July 2023, as market probability of an October move has fallen to 24%. Meanwhile, the unofficial start of a new earnings season arrives with 12 companies holding market caps over $1 billion scheduled to report, including Pepsi and Delta Air Lines. Traders also monitor an economic calendar featuring global PMI data, U.S. Jobless Claims, and the Michigan Consumer Sentiment reading.

items.title: Commodity weekly: Broad losses mask persistent supply risks
items.excerpt: Key Points: Commodities retreat broadly, with the BCOM Total Return Index down 2.1% as improving crude flows, harvest pressure and tighter financial conditions weigh on prices. Fuel shortages persist despite recovering crude supply, with potential emergency stock releases easing diesel prices while refinery disruptions and restricted exports constrain availability. Metals face competing pressures, as higher yields weigh on gold despite resilient ETF demand, while copper s retreat leaves tight availability outside the US unresolved. Weather risks lift sugar and coffee, with El Ni o threatening agricultural supply while grains face harvest pressure and speculative selling. Commodities traded broadly lower this week as a challenging macro backdrop outweighed persistent physical tightness…

items.title: Euro FX futures slide to 16-month lows as dollar finds support.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures extend their decline for a fourth consecutive session, falling roughly 0.75% to 1.1274 and marking their lowest levels since mid-May 2025. The selloff is primarily driven by sustained strength in the U.S. dollar, which remains near the top of its recent range despite a downward shift across the Treasury yield curve following comments from Federal Reserve officials. Additional pressure on the euro stems from ongoing inflationary and energy-related concerns in the eurozone heading into the winter months. Broad dollar strength is also weighing on other major currencies, with the British pound sliding toward its lows for the year and the Australian dollar facing renewed pressure, while the Japanese yen remains bound within its multi-month range.

items.title: Q4 Outlook for Investors: Raise the bar
items.excerpt: Our Q4 base case is a volatile upward grind, but with much greater dispersion beneath the index. Key points: AI meets expensive money: AI spending can remain strong, but higher funding costs, rapid obsolescence and rising reinvestment needs will increasingly separate companies that can comfortably finance the AI race from those spending simply to stay competitive. Inflation needs more than one hedge: Oil is only part of the risk. El Ni o, fiscal spending and the AI infrastructure buildout could also keep pressure on food, power, commodities and bond yields. Bonds are competitive again: With the US 10-year Treasury yield around 5%, investors no longer need to rely as heavily on equities for returns. items.title: Euro futures drop to lowest level since mid-July as dollar gains.
items.excerpt: Euro futures traded lower, reaching 1.1350 before closing near 1.1365, marking the lowest level since mid-July. The decline was driven by U.S. dollar strength following rising inflation expectations and shifting Federal Reserve rate hike expectations. The euro has fallen approximately 3% since its August peak above 1.17. Meanwhile, option-derived volatility increased alongside the market decline, as measured by the CVOL index. Speculators expanded their net short positions last week, extending a continuous net short posture in euro futures since late June.
